findings.title: Retry signs fresh 402 requirements without comparing to what the user approved
findings.evidence: src/browser/useStellarPayment.ts:99 `const retryPayload = await client.createPaymentPayload(freshRequirements);` · src/browser/useStellarPayment.ts:62 `const paymentPayload = await client.createPaymentPayload(paymentRequired);` · src/browser/StellarPaywall.tsx:153 `if (Number(freshBalance) < amount) {`

findings.title: Paywall displays a server-supplied amount that is not the amount that gets signed
Any non-testnet stellar:* network is labelled "Stellar Mainnet"
Paid response HTML written to documentElement.innerHTML
Server-injected RPC URL and network drive signing

failing_checks.title: Per-action amount bound
failing_checks.reason: No maximum is enforced before signing. The retry signs whatever amount the 402 response states. The only check, a balance comparison, covers neither the retry nor an upper bound.

failing_checks.title: Cumulative budget
failing_checks.reason: No cumulative budget exists. Each signature depends only on a wallet prompt.

failing_checks.title: Recipient binding
failing_checks.reason: The payee comes from the server's 402 response, including the retry's fresh requirements. No allowlist or binding to the approved payTo exists.

failing_checks.title: Asset identity and units
failing_checks.reason: The balance check uses a float Number, and x402.amount (injected config) takes precedence over the requirement's amount. The signed value comes from paymentRequired, and on retry from the fresh requirements, so the checked and signed values can differ.

failing_checks.title: Replay and double payment
failing_checks.reason: After the first signed payload is sent and the server returns a 402, the code signs a second payload with no idempotency check. Both payloads may be valid, so the payer can be charged twice.

failing_checks.title: Externally supplied transactions
failing_checks.reason: The retry signs requirements taken from a 402 response without comparing payTo, amount, asset or network to what the user approved. The first call also signs paymentRequired as injected, with no inspection of the simulated auth tree.

failing_checks.title: Network and endpoint pinning
failing_checks.reason: The RPC URL comes from window.x402.config.rpcUrl, which the paywalled server injects. The scheme is registered for every stellar:* network, so the 402 response, including the retry, picks the network. A malicious server can point the simulation at its own RPC and return arbitrary auth entries. useSt

failing_checks.title: Approvals fail closed
failing_checks.reason: After a 402 response, the retry path signs fresh server-supplied terms. The user never saw or approved them, and nothing compares them to the approved amount, asset or payee. Only the first signature comes from the user's click.

failing_checks.title: Outbound requests and file paths
failing_checks.reason: The RPC URL comes from the server-injected window.x402.config.rpcUrl and is not checked against an allowlist. The paywall page's own server controls it.

failing_checks.title: Controls outside the prompt
failing_checks.reason: No code compares the retry requirements (payTo, amount, asset, network) with what the user approved. The server's fresh 402 is signed as received.
